item.title: Dramatic death of Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) caught on camera — Space photo of the week
item.description: The Gemini North telescope snapped a spectacular view of Comet C/2025 K1 (ATLAS) breaking apart as it emerged from the other side of the sun in October.

item.title: Physicists push quantum boundaries by turning a superfluid into a supersolid — and back — for the first time
item.description: Physicists saw excitons, a type of quasiparticle, undergo a reversible phase transition from superfluid to supersolid for the first time, opening new doors for studying extreme states of matter.

item.title: Microbes in Iceland are hoarding nitrogen, and that's mucking up the nutrient cycle
item.description: A study in Iceland found that microbes are hoarding more nitrogen for themselves, altering nutrient cycling and leaving less for plants.

item.title: 'Night owls' may have worse heart health — but why?
item.description: Emerging evidence suggests that "night owls" are more likely to have poor heart health and a higher risk of heart attack or stroke than "morning larks." Why is that?

item.title: Paleo-Inuit people braved icy seas to reach remote Greenland islands 4,500 years ago, archaeologists discover
item.description: Archaeological remains on the Kitsissut islands off the coast of Greenland reveal that whole communities regularly journeyed across the dangerous Arctic waters.

item.title: Sandals of Tutankhamun: 3,300-year-old footwear that let King Tut walk all over his enemies
item.description: Among the sandals discovered in Tut's tomb is a pair whose insoles were decorated with images of the boy king's enemies.

item.title: The best toddler-friendly air purifier we have tested is now at its lowest-ever price
item.description: Save $100 on the Levoit Sprout, an excellent all-in-one appliance that combines an air purifier, a night light and a white noise machine.

item.title: Impossibly powerful 'ghost particle' that slammed into Earth may have come from an exploding black hole — and it could upend both particle physics and cosmology
item.description: A supercharged neutrino that smashed into our planet in 2023 may have been spit out by an exploding primordial black hole with a "dark charge." If true, this theory could lead to a definitive catalog of all subatomic particles and unveil the elusive identity of dark matter.

item.title: New 'sungrazing' comet could become visible to the naked eye during the day — if the sun doesn't destroy it
item.description: The newly discovered sungrazing comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS) will undergo an extremely close slingshot around our star in early April, and could become bright enough to be seen without a telescope during the day.

item.title: Viking Age mass grave holds mysterious mix of dismembered human remains and complete skeletons, including a 'giant' who'd had brain surgery
item.description: Archaeologists and student excavators uncovered a Viking Age pit full of dismembered remains near Cambridge, England.
